main_text.l: SCilicet,obscurè fueras,Rex doćte,locutus, (Dum caneres multis omnia vana modis) Vt quàm multus agit toto mortalis in orbe, Tam fit clarator multus in orbe tuus.
Rex,seruus,sapiens,stultus,iuuenífque senéxque, Diues,honoratus,pauper,honoris egens, In rebus clamant hominum nil præter inane: Vanáque non vané cunćta perire docent.
Omnia vana docent omneis interprete linguá: Mente manúque docent omnia vana simul.
Quin ego,cunćta queror qui multus inania,inanis Mente,manu,linguâ,cógito,scribo,loquor.
Attamen est ratio,vani quâ nomen & omen Diffugiat, solidi fons maneátque boni.
Numinis obsequio natum sc nosse,beato Illius & fœtum pećtus habere metu, Est firmum vitæ nunquam nutantis asylum: Nil & inane subest,hoc vbi munus adest.

page.notes: The woodcut ornament at the top and the marginal fragments on the right edge are not transcribed. Some letters in the poem are blurred; the readings above are the most likely ones. The signature line "ANTONIVS FAYVS." is set in small capitals and is treated as a closing line, not a heading.
